subject: Clarify: Uptime counting for multi-provider routing during ChainLink outage
messages:
From: Alex Torres <ops@metrogrid.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@metrogrid.com
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 07:12:00 -0700
Subject: Partial degradation in us-east (seen as downstream provider flap) — request for credit guidance

Hi Stephanie,

Our SRE team observed a sustained elevation in 5xxs and latency for requests routed through the us-east cluster between 2026-08-22T09:40:00Z and 2026-08-22T10:22:00Z. Traces indicate a downstream carrier (ChainLink) experienced a regional flap and several of our requests were routed through that provider.

Two quick asks:
- Please confirm how Redwood counts uptime in scenarios where a third-party network/provider experiences an outage that affects a subset of routed traffic.
- If this meets SLA credit criteria, what is the process and expected timeline for applying a credit? We will need documentation for our internal auditors.

Attaching a short sample trace for your review.

Thanks,
Alex Torres
SRE Lead, MetroGrid Energy

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Partial degradation in us-east — need engineering & support calc

Team, forwarding MetroGrid's note. They asked specifically how we count uptime when only a subset of traffic is impacted by a downstream provider.

Questions I need answered before I reply:
- Do we treat this as an "infrastructure incident" eligible for SLA credit, or is it excluded as a third-party/peering event per our TOS?
- If eligible, what's the right apportionment approach (simple time-window vs. weighted by affected requests)?
- What logs/traces do we need from them to reproduce and substantiate the claim?

Can someone take point? I want a clear, customer-friendly explanation and a proposed next step (credit + call or denial + explanation).

Thanks — Steph

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Partial degradation in us-east — need engineering & support calc

Steph — quick technical summary:

What happened (short): our smart routing attempted alternate peers when the primary peering path to ChainLink degraded. A fraction (~22%) of MetroGrid's requests were routed through that flapping peer during the window 2026-08-22T09:40:00Z–2026-08-22T10:22:00Z. Error spike was mostly 502/504 and latency > 1s for those requests.

SLA wording & approach: our current SLA excludes "third-party backbone or peering" events if the root cause is outside Redwood's routing/compute layer. However, the contract also states that if Redwood's routing decisions (e.g., using a degraded peer without graceful fallback) contributed, we can apportion credit.

Suggested apportionment: compute the fraction of MetroGrid's total successful token/time volume that experienced degraded responses during the window and apply that fraction to the downtime metric — i.e., "weighted downtime". Practically:
- numerator = count(requests_by_metrogrid that returned 5xx or latency>threshold routed via the affected peer during window)
- denominator = total requests_by_metrogrid in the same window across all routes

Data required: full routing trace (which MetroGrid provided a sample of) + our server-side routing logs and KV cache stats so we can show retries/alternate serving. If the trace shows that Redwood retried and successfully served many requests from cache without failing, that reduces the effective downtime.

I'll pull logs and run a quick count. If we see >5% of their traffic impacted with no successful fallback, recommend offering pro-rated credit.

— Rishi

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ops@metrogrid.com
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Partial degradation in us-east — need engineering & support calc

Hi all, attaching my initial calculations and routing trace export (metrogrid_routing_trace.csv). Summary:

- Window inspected: 2026-08-22T09:40:00Z — 2026-08-22T10:22:00Z
- MetroGrid total requests in window: 18,420
- Requests routed via affected peer: 4,062 (22.05%)
- Of those routed via affected peer, errors or latency>1s: 3,874
- Effective impacted requests (no successful response after retries): 1,271

Using Rishi's weighted approach: impacted fraction = 1,271 / 18,420 = 6.9%

Given our SLA threshold for credit is downtime that causes >=5% of customer request volume to be affected during the billing period, this crosses the threshold. However, because a routing peer outside our managed infrastructure contributed to the root cause, legal/TOS review is required before committing a credit.

Attachments: metrogrid_routing_trace.csv (attachment stub), redwood_uptime_calc_notes.pdf (attachment stub: calculation worksheet).

If legal gives the OK, I recommend we offer a pro-rata credit equivalent to 6.9% of the per-day usage charge for 2026-08-22 and document the computation.

— Sean

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <ops@metrogrid.com>
Cc: legal@metrogrid.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Partial degradation in us-east (seen as downstream provider flap) — request for credit guidance

Alex — thanks for the original report and for the sample traces. We reviewed the incident end-to-end. Short version: our internal analysis indicates ~6.9% of MetroGrid's requests during the impacted window were not successfully served after retries, which would exceed the SLA credit threshold. Because the root cause involved a downstream provider (ChainLink) and some traffic was routed through an external peer, we need a brief legal review to confirm eligibility under the contract exclusion clauses.

Proposed next steps:
1) Legal review (we've looped in our contracts team) — ETA 48 business hours.
2) If approved, we will apply a pro-rated credit equal to 6.9% of MetroGrid's Redwood usage for 2026-08-22; we will provide a calculation worksheet and signed acknowledgement.
3) Optional: I'll schedule a technical follow-up call this week to walk through the traces and discuss routing hardening options (preferred: shorten peer failover window and increase cache retention for critical customers).

We have shared the raw trace export and our calculation worksheet here: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/metrogrid/traces/2026-08-22. If you'd like to move forward with the credit, please confirm and we'll circulate a DocuSign for an SLA credit addendum.

Thanks,
Steph
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
